segments.flavor: the station ID / sweeper, and it ends with a rewind
segments.text:
Vance: [cheerful] Cassette! Big hair, bigger chorus, and a countdown to absolutely nothing.
Vance: Number one with a bullet, forever. Rewind and go.

segments.flavor: the station ID / sweeper, and it ends with a rewind
segments.text:
Vance: You are locked into Cassette, where the tape never wears out and the chorus never quits.
Vance: Hold the hairspray. Here comes the song.

segments.flavor: the station ID / sweeper, and it ends with a rewind
segments.text:
Vance: [shouting] This is Cassette! Everything is loud, everything is neon, everything repeats.
Vance: Roll the tape back and hit play.

segments.flavor: the station ID / sweeper, and it ends with a rewind
segments.text:
Vance: Cassette. Home of the drum sound that knocks doors off their hinges.
Vance: Ingrid says it is a preset. Ingrid is right. Rewind, and play it.

segments.flavor: Vance turns something ordinary into a countdown and commits fully
segments.text:
Vance: Tonight's weather, in reverse order. At number three, a breeze. Number two, one cloud.
Vance: Holding at number one for the ninth straight night — dark. Play the record.

segments.flavor: Vance turns something ordinary into a countdown and commits fully
segments.text:
Vance: The hours are charting tonight. Midnight is climbing. One in the morning is falling fast.
Vance: And four in the morning is a new entry, straight in at the top. Music!

segments.flavor: Ingrid names the exact drum machine or synth on the last record; Vance takes it personally
segments.text:
Vance: That snare. That is a wall coming down. Nobody ever built a snare like it.
Ingrid: Drum machine, factory bank, gated reverb. Nine studios built it that same week.
Vance: Nine? Roll the next one.

segments.flavor: Boyd calls from a payphone with big news and runs out of coins before the point
segments.text:
Vance: Boyd is calling from the payphone. Boyd, the big news, go.
Boyd: Vance, I have carried this all week, and the thing about it is —
Boyd: Hang on. The machine is eating my —
Ingrid: Coins.
Vance: Gone. Play the song.

segments.flavor: Vance turns something ordinary into a countdown and commits fully
segments.text:
Vance: Here is tonight's studio coffee chart. At number three, this morning's cup, still warm, still climbing.
Vance: At two, the pot itself. New entry at the top, with a bullet: the plastic spoon. Hit the music.

segments.flavor: Vance turns something ordinary into a countdown and commits fully
segments.text:
Vance: Tonight my jacket is a chart. At number two, the zipper, which climbed all week and stuck.
Vance: And number one, with a bullet, immovable: the shoulders. Nothing beats the shoulders. Straight into the song.

segments.flavor: back-announce the last record as this week's number one with a bullet; Ingrid corrects the year
segments.text:
Vance: That record is this hour's number one with a bullet. Undisputed.
Ingrid: It charted twice. The first time was six years before you think.
Vance: Six? I was there. I had a scarf.
Ingrid: You had a scarf both times. Here comes the next one.

segments.flavor: Ingrid names the exact drum machine or synth on the last record; Vance takes it personally
segments.text:
Vance: That bass. That is a real player. You can hear fingers on the strings.
Ingrid: That is a synth. One oscillator, one filter sweep, no fingers at all.
Vance: [sigh] There are always fingers, Ingrid.
Ingrid: Not this time. Roll the tape.

segments.flavor: Ingrid names the exact drum machine or synth on the last record; Vance takes it personally
segments.text:
Vance: Those handclaps! A whole room of people clapping at once. You can feel the room.
Ingrid: Twelve claps, sampled once, retriggered. One person, one afternoon, one machine.
Vance: One person? That is a party of one.
Ingrid: It was a Tuesday. He clapped once and went to lunch.
Vance: I respect him more now. Next record, go.

segments.flavor: back-announce the last record as this week's number one with a bullet; Ingrid corrects the year
segments.text:
Vance: New at the top with a bullet — that one. A monster. A giant.
Ingrid: It is a giant. It is also four years older than you announced.
Vance: I round the years down. It keeps the whole chart feeling young.
Ingrid: Nothing on this chart is young. Not even the chorus.
Vance: The chorus is eternal! Into the next record now.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for hairspray, sincere eighties announcer grammar, rapid disclaimer from Ingrid
segments.text:
Vance: Cassette is brought to you by Monolith Hold hairspray.
Ingrid: [serious] Monolith Hold.
Vance: One pass, and your hair is a building. Wind does nothing. Doors bounce off.
Ingrid: Monolith Hold is flammable, permanent, and not approved for use near a candle.
Vance: It smells like victory and lemon. Ask for the black can.
Ingrid: Do not ask for the black can. Here comes the chorus.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a car phone, sincere eighties announcer grammar, rapid disclaimer from Ingrid
segments.text:
Vance: The Cordova Car Phone. A telephone. In your car. Think about that.
Ingrid: It weighs as much as a small dog and costs a great deal more.
Vance: Call the office from a parking lot. Call your mother from a bridge.
Ingrid: Range is forty feet. The bridge must be very close to the house.
Vance: Cordova. Because the future has a curly cord.
Ingrid: Antenna sold separately. Straight into the next song.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a home video system, sincere eighties announcer grammar, rapid disclaimer from Ingrid
segments.text:
Vance: The Panorama Four Hundred home video system. Top loading. Wood grain. Four heads.
Ingrid: Nobody knows what the fourth head does.
Vance: Record one show while you watch another show. Live in two places at once.
Ingrid: You will record the wrong channel. Everybody records the wrong channel.
Vance: The remote is attached by a cable, and that cable is thirty feet long.
Ingrid: Trip hazard. Not our fault. Here comes the record.

segments.flavor: the Countdown To Nothing
segments.text:
Vance: It is time for the Countdown To Nothing! Are you ready? Nobody is ready.
Ingrid: Nobody has ever been ready.
Vance: Five! Four! Three! Two! One!
Ingrid: And nothing.
Vance: Nothing! Beautiful, perfect nothing. Every hour, on the hour, we count down to it.
Ingrid: Why do we do this?
Vance: Because a countdown has to land somewhere, and nothing never disappoints.
Ingrid: That is almost wisdom.
Vance: It is entirely wisdom. Now, the opposite of nothing — this record.

segments.flavor: Name That Preset, the guessing game Vance always loses
segments.text:
Ingrid: Time for Name That Preset. I describe a sound. You name the machine.
Vance: I was born for this. Give me the sound.
Ingrid: A metal tube being hit in a stairwell, but polite about it.
Vance: A real metal tube in a real stairwell. Final answer. Lock it in.
Ingrid: It is a factory preset. Bank two. It is called Steel Drum.
Vance: Steel Drum is a place, Ingrid. It is a beach.
Ingrid: It is a slider on a machine in a cold room.
Vance: You have ruined the beach.
Ingrid: I have explained the beach.
Vance: Same thing. Next round after this record.

segments.flavor: the ex-wife report, who is doing great, apparently
segments.text:
Vance: And now, the part of the show I insist on. The ex-wife report.
Ingrid: [sigh] You do insist, yes.
Vance: She is doing great. Apparently. That is the whole report.
Ingrid: Who tells you this?
Vance: Everyone tells me this. Strangers tell me this. The man at the counter told me.
Ingrid: And how are you doing, Vance?
Vance: I am on the radio with big hair and a countdown. I am thriving.
Ingrid: That was almost convincing.
Vance: It was completely convincing. Here comes a loud one.

segments.flavor: Boyd calls from a payphone with big news and runs out of coins before the point
segments.text:
Vance: Boyd! From the payphone on the corner. What is the big news tonight?
Boyd: This one is big, Vance. I have been sitting on it since Sunday.
Ingrid: Sit faster, Boyd.
Boyd: So I opened the garage, and behind the mower there was a —
Vance: There was a what? Boyd?
Ingrid: He is out of coins again.
Vance: The garage keeps its mower and its secret. Back to the music.

segments.flavor: Vance turns something ordinary into a countdown and commits fully
segments.text:
Vance: I rode the elevator up tonight and counted it back down. Floor three, a strong debut.
Ingrid: Vance, that is an elevator. Not a chart.
Vance: Floor two held steady. And floor one, this studio, is number one with a bullet.
Ingrid: The building has four floors. You skipped one entirely.
Vance: Floor four is next week's chart. Take it away, tape deck.

segments.flavor: Ingrid names the exact drum machine or synth on the last record; Vance takes it personally
segments.text:
Vance: That choir at the end. A hundred voices. A cathedral. Goosebumps on the goosebumps.
Ingrid: One singer, four takes, a chorus pedal and a very patient engineer.
Vance: A hundred voices, Ingrid. I counted them myself.
Ingrid: You did not. Nobody counts a hundred voices at that speed.
Vance: I counted the feeling of them, which is the same number.
Ingrid: The cathedral is a preset. It is called Large Hall.
Vance: Large Hall is my favorite building in the world. Cue the song.

segments.flavor: back-announce the last record as this week's number one with a bullet; Ingrid corrects the year
segments.text:
Vance: That was the number one record in the country, with a bullet, and it still is.
Ingrid: It was number eleven. For one week. In one small country.
Vance: Eleven rounds up.
Ingrid: Eleven does not round up to one anywhere, Vance.
Vance: It does with the right attitude and a strong spotlight.
Ingrid: Your year is also wrong by about three summers.
Vance: My years are approximate. My enthusiasm is exact.
Ingrid: [sigh] Approximate is a generous word for it.
Vance: I chose it myself. Give me a chorus.

segments.flavor: Boyd calls from a payphone with big news and runs out of coins before the point
segments.text:
Vance: Payphone line! Boyd, you sound like you are standing in a wind tunnel.
Boyd: It is the road, Vance. Big truck. Anyway, the news. Are you sitting?
Ingrid: We are always sitting. It is radio.
Boyd: I found the thing. The thing I told you about in the spring.
Vance: The thing! He found the thing! Boyd, what is the thing?
Boyd: It was under the — hold on, I have one more coin, I —
Ingrid: And the coin is gone.
Vance: The thing remains a mystery. On with the music.

segments.flavor: Vance turns something ordinary into a countdown and commits fully
segments.text:
Vance: Tonight's traffic light chart. At number three, the light on Ninth. Slow, moody, a grower.
Ingrid: A grower.
Vance: At number two, the blinking one nobody obeys. Reckless, exciting, very now.
Ingrid: And number one is red, I assume.
Vance: Red! Red has been number one for forty weeks. Red is a legend.
Ingrid: Red is a lamp, Vance. You waited at all three tonight.
Vance: I waited at all three and I enjoyed every single second.
Ingrid: That explains the mood you came in with.
Vance: The mood is called anticipation. Here is the song.

segments.flavor: Ingrid names the exact drum machine or synth on the last record; Vance takes it personally
segments.text:
Vance: That saxophone. A man in a coat on a fire escape at midnight. Real brass.
Ingrid: It is brass. It is also doubled by a keyboard playing the same line.
Vance: No.
Ingrid: Yes. The keyboard is louder than the saxophone in the mix.
Vance: You are telling me the man in the coat had help.
Ingrid: The man in the coat had a keyboard player standing behind him.
Vance: Was the keyboard player also wearing a coat?
Ingrid: [chuckle] Nobody ever asks that. Probably a cardigan.
Vance: A cardigan. The romance is gone, Ingrid. Completely gone.
Ingrid: The solo is still beautiful, cardigan and all.
Vance: It is. Play the next one, quickly.

segments.flavor: back-announce the last record as this week's number one with a bullet; Ingrid corrects the year
segments.text:
Vance: Straight in at number one with a bullet. That is the sound of a bullet.
Ingrid: A bullet is not a sound. And that record is nine years older than you said.
Vance: The chart is a living thing, Ingrid. It breathes. It moves.
Ingrid: The chart is a list. Lists do not breathe.
Vance: Mine does. Mine has lungs and a haircut.
Ingrid: A haircut is not a chart feature.
Vance: On this station the haircut is the whole feature.
Ingrid: Your chart had the weather at number two last night.
Vance: The weather is a strong performer. Consistent. Reliable. Very moody.
Ingrid: You are describing a sky.
Vance: I am describing a star. Next record, please.

segments.flavor: Boyd calls from a payphone with big news and runs out of coins before the point
segments.text:
Vance: Boyd is back at the payphone. Boyd, tell me you brought coins tonight.
Boyd: A whole bag of them, Vance. Heavy bag. Very heavy bag.
Ingrid: That is a first.
Boyd: So, the news. You know the shop on the corner with the awning?
Vance: The green awning, or the one that used to be green?
Ingrid: There are two awnings in this story already.
Boyd: The one that used to be green. A truck pulled up, and out came —
Vance: Out came what? Boyd? The bag, Boyd, use the bag!
Ingrid: The bag was full of buttons. I could hear it.
Vance: Somebody sold that man a sack of buttons.
Ingrid: And the awning keeps its secret another week.
Vance: The awning wins again. Let the tape roll.

segments.flavor: Vance turns something ordinary into a countdown and commits fully
segments.text:
Vance: Big one tonight. The seasons, ranked, counted down, no appeals accepted.
Ingrid: The seasons.
Vance: At four, winter. Too long, poor chorus, terrible for the hair.
Ingrid: Hair is a category now.
Vance: Hair is the only category. At three, spring. Wet, ambitious, hair collapses.
Ingrid: Collapses.
Vance: Completely. It is a hard season for a working professional.
Ingrid: You are the only professional you have in mind.
Vance: At two, autumn. Big coat, big sky, tremendous hair.
Ingrid: And summer takes it.
Vance: Summer, number one with a bullet, and it always will be.
Vance: Because of the convertibles, obviously. Now, the number one record. Play it.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a waterbed showroom, sincere eighties announcer grammar, rapid disclaimer from Ingrid
segments.text:
Vance: Lagoon Waterbeds. Sleep on a lake, indoors, without a single fish.
Ingrid: A lake weighs a great deal. Ask about your floor first.
Vance: Heated. Padded. Available in six shades of brown.
Ingrid: Six shades of brown is not a choice, it is a mood.
Vance: Lagoon. Come in and float away from your troubles.
Ingrid: Do not float away with a cat present. Music, now.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for an aerobics videotape, sincere eighties announcer grammar, rapid disclaimer from Ingrid
segments.text:
Vance: New from our sponsors, the Thunder Aerobics tape. Ninety minutes. One leotard. No mercy.
Ingrid: Ninety minutes is longer than most people are alive on a Monday.
Vance: Grapevine. Lunge. Reach for something that is not there. Feel the burn!
Ingrid: The burn is your carpet. The tape does not cover carpet damage.
Vance: Comes with a headband in a color that does not exist in nature.
Ingrid: Neon is not a color. It is a warning. Back to the record.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for an answering machine, sincere eighties announcer grammar, rapid disclaimer from Ingrid
segments.text:
Vance: The Messenger Nine answering machine. Two tapes. One tiny speaker. Infinite possibility.
Ingrid: One tape records your greeting badly. The other loses the message.
Vance: Never miss a call again. Come home to a blinking red light.
Ingrid: The blinking red light is usually your uncle. It is always your uncle.
Vance: The Messenger Nine. Because you are a busy and important person.
Ingrid: You are not. Nobody is. Back into the music.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a tanning salon, sincere eighties announcer grammar, rapid disclaimer from Ingrid
segments.text:
Vance: Solarium Ten. Ten lamps. Ten minutes. One extremely confident color.
Ingrid: The color has a name. The name is orange.
Vance: Walk in pale. Walk out like a man who owns a boat.
Ingrid: He does not own a boat. He owns ten minutes of regret.
Vance: First session is free with any hairspray purchase.
Ingrid: Goggles are not optional, whatever the sign says. Back to the songs.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a personal stereo, sincere eighties announcer grammar, rapid disclaimer from Ingrid
segments.text:
Vance: Pocket Thunder. A whole stereo, on your belt, running on four batteries.
Ingrid: Four batteries lasting roughly one bus ride.
Vance: Orange foam headphones. Metal clip. A belt clip that has never once held.
Ingrid: The clip is decorative. The sidewalk gets the player eventually.
Vance: Pocket Thunder. Because music should follow you out the door.
Ingrid: Bring a spare clip and a broom. On with the song.

segments.flavor: the Video Vault, shot by shot, with Ingrid on the budget
segments.text:
Vance: Open the Video Vault! Picture it. A hallway. Fog. One door at the end.
Ingrid: The fog is a machine rented by the hour.
Vance: The door opens. The band is inside, playing on a floor made of light.
Ingrid: That floor is plywood with lamps underneath. Two lamps failed during the shoot.
Vance: A wind arrives from nowhere. Every coat moves as one coat.
Ingrid: One fan. Borrowed. Returned late.
Vance: The singer walks toward the camera and the hallway goes on forever.
Ingrid: The hallway was eleven feet long. They filmed it four times.
Vance: Eleven feet of pure eternity. That is the Video Vault. Back to the chorus.

segments.flavor: the Rewind, a live show played backward on request
segments.text:
Vance: You know what this show needs? A rewind. Hold on. Here it comes.
Ingrid: We cannot rewind a live show, Vance.
Vance: We can rewind anything. Watch me. Everything I said is going backward now.
Ingrid: You are just saying words in a different order.
Vance: Order different a in words saying just are you.
Ingrid: [chuckle] Fine. That was a rewind.
Vance: The Rewind. Every night, at no particular time, for no particular reason.
Ingrid: It is the only feature with a sound effect and no point.
Vance: Points are for the news. Let the music back in.

segments.flavor: the hair check, a studio report on volume
segments.text:
Vance: Hair check! Ingrid, how is the hair tonight?
Ingrid: My hair is fine. It is hair. It sits there.
Vance: Wrong answer. Hair does not sit. Hair arrives. Hair announces you.
Ingrid: Mine announces nothing. Mine is a rumor.
Vance: Mine is visible from the parking structure. Two people asked me for directions.
Ingrid: Directions to where?
Vance: To me. They were already there. That is the power of volume.
Ingrid: That is the power of standing under a light.
Vance: Same power, different source. Hair check complete. Give me that record.

segments.flavor: the studio address book, where a record was cut
segments.text:
Ingrid: Studio address book. That record was cut in a converted grain store by a river.
Vance: A river! With a little bridge and a boat and a man fishing?
Ingrid: With a loading dock and a broken window they never fixed.
Vance: I am picturing a holiday. I am packing already.
Ingrid: The room was cold. The engineer wore two coats indoors.
Vance: A cozy river holiday with coats. It gets better every second.
Ingrid: The reverb you love is that cold room. That is all it is.
Vance: Then the room is my favorite destination. Music, please.

segments.flavor: Mixtape Corner, the rules of a tape
segments.text:
Vance: Mixtape Corner. Rule one. The first song must arrive like a door kicked open.
Ingrid: Rule one is fine. Rule two is where you go wrong.
Vance: Rule two! The slow one goes at the end of side one. Always.
Ingrid: Then you have four minutes of blank tape and a click.
Vance: Blank tape is drama. Blank tape is the intermission.
Ingrid: Blank tape is arithmetic you did not do.
Vance: Rule three. Never label a side until the tape is finished.
Ingrid: You never label them at all. That is why they are all mysteries.
Vance: Every tape should be a mystery. Side one, track one. Go!
